amendments.body: Fix `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:575-624`: `molt_cycle()` checks `readiness = timer_days / effective_interval` before incrementing `molt_timer_days`, then increments the timer after the resolution branch. A cohort that starts at `0.0` therefore resolves on daily step `interval + 1` instead of on the configured interval (for example, a 28-day adult interval resolves on day 29, and a 14-day juvenile interval resolves on day 15). That makes the species cadence parameters systematically one day slower than the values in data. Either increment the timers before the readiness check or compute readiness from the post-step timer.
amendments.rationale: This is a runtime correctness bug in the new per-stage molt cadence, and the current tests only check relative stage ordering, so the off-by-one can slip through unnoticed.

amendments.body: Fix the mismatch between the modeled high-GH penalty and the failure diagnostics. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1389-1400` reduces `molt_mineral_modifier()` when `gh_d > gh_max_d`, which can push a healthy shrimp below `molt_success_threshold`. But `emit_molt_failure()` at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1180-1232` only reports low GH/Ca/Mg and otherwise falls back to `PoorCondition`, so a very hard-water failure can be logged as `condition 1.00` even though the modeled driver was excessive GH. Either surface a high-GH/high-mineral diagnostic or remove the above-range GH penalty from the molt mechanic.
amendments.rationale: Right now the implementation can produce a player-visible explanation that contradicts the actual branch that failed the molt check.

amendments.body: Re-tighten `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:1095-1118`. This test explicitly disables shrimp mortality at `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:1048-1049`, but the updated day-60/day-90 envelopes now accept `shrimp_count(0, ...)`, `juveniles_count(0, ...)`, and zero reproductive readiness. That means a total colony collapse after an early hatch pulse would still satisfy the checkpoint envelopes, materially weakening the regression that is supposed to guard the controlled ideal reproduction path. Restore non-zero floors at those checkpoints.
amendments.rationale: This is a significant regression-test weakening: the named scenario can now pass after behavior that should be impossible under its own setup.

payload.summary: Reviewed the molt/mineral implementation and its updated save/load and scenario coverage. Targeted `tank_core` and `tank_harness` tests pass, but I found three remaining issues: the new per-stage molt cadence is off by one day, high-GH-induced molt failures are misdiagnosed as poor condition, and the controlled-reproduction e2e guard was loosened enough to miss catastrophic regressions.
